=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** Disregard it. The [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is the Seller's own characterisation; nothing in our record shows the Buyer has "reviewed and cleared" or "accepted" any of these positions. The note is an attempt to narrow our review, and in fact every clause tagged [STANDARD] is adverse to the Buyer. All 16 items below are treated as open.

Also note the disclosure letter is dated against a data room cut-off of 22 September 2026 — now over six weeks stale. Require a bring-down to signing and again to Completion.

---

| # | Issue | Seller's position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) | Higher general cap (target 50–100%; floor 30%), with specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) and fundamental/tax warranties **outside** the cap | **Reject.** 20% is at the low end and the known-issue exposure (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, Riverlark 3.2m) already approaches it. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | De minimis 25k; basket 250k; excess-only (deductible) | De minimis ~10k; basket ~0.5–1% of price (120–240k) on a **tipping** (first-dollar) basis; thresholds not to apply to specific indemnities, fundamental or tax claims | **Counter.** Deductible basket plus high de minimis on a 24m deal is above market and erodes a meaningful slice of recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); longer periods for tax (statute of limitations + 6–12 months) and fundamentals (6–7 years); delete the "applies to all Claims" default | **Counter.** 18 months is short and the default-sweep language silently imports every limitation into indemnity and fundamental claims. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year claim period, outside de minimis/basket | **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20% cap on being sold shares the Seller does not own. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | None offered; limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Express carve-out: no limitation (cap, threshold, time, knowledge, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance) applies to fraud, wilful concealment or dishonesty of the Seller or its officers | **Insist.** A regime that purports to cap fraud is unacceptable and likely unenforceable in any event — put it in the drafting. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, registers and all public searchable records | Only matters **fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no disclosure of public records beyond specified ASIC/PPSR/IP searches; no disclosure against fundamental warranties or specific indemnities | **Reject.** Blanket data-room and public-record disclosure converts the warranty package into near-zero protection. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records | Delete; at most, limited to actual knowledge of 3–4 named deal-team individuals of specific matters, with a bring-down of DD findings into specific indemnities | **Reject.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge is a constructive-knowledge bar that neutralises the warranties entirely. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent | Hard condition precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent (cl 11.2) **with evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived**; best endeavours; Buyer-controlled waiver; MAC/price adjustment if lost | **Reject the framing.** Disclosure letter ¶2 admits no consent exists for a ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% revenue contract — "addressed" is untrue. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Repayment and full discharge of security (cl 9.2) **at Completion** via funds flow, with payout letter and PPSR release as completion deliverables; waiver of cl 8.1 change-of-control; debt deducted in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics | **Reject.** A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt in default under the change-of-control clause. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow | Bonuses plus super, payroll tax and on-costs treated as Debt / Transaction Costs in the price mechanics or paid by Seller pre-Completion; specific indemnity; itemised in funds flow | **Reject.** They are triggered by Completion, so the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) bears them unless the mechanics say otherwise. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Seller pays the AUD 180k and delivers receipt + confirmatory assignment **as a completion deliverable**; indemnity covers all loss from any failure of title to Project Materials (not just the fee), uncapped and outside thresholds | **Counter.** Under cl 7.3 the IP does not transfer until payment clears, so the exposure is loss of IP, not just a 180k invoice. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident | "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material | Specific indemnity for all costs (investigation, OAIC notification, remediation, third-party claims, regulatory penalties) uncapped or separately capped; warranty that investigation is complete and notifications made; pre-Completion completion of investigation | **Reject.** ~1,240 personal records sent to an unknown external party is a potential notifiable data breach and the investigation was "preliminary" six weeks ago — the Seller cannot both not know the scope and assert immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary-course operating costs | Determine whether each of the 3 × AUD 110k is accrued/committed; treat accrued or Seller-triggered amounts as Debt or working-capital adjustment; warranty on no non-ordinary-course commitments; confirm terminability | **Counter.** Seller's own disclosure (¶8) declines to say they are ordinary course, so the Seller's cover note is unsupported. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | One regime for everything (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; "all Claims of any nature") | Distinct regimes: (i) general warranties; (ii) fundamental; (iii) tax; (iv) specific indemnities; (v) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and period; exclusive-remedy and non-reliance not to limit indemnities, fraud or equitable relief | **Reject.** Collapsing categories means the 20%/18-month/basket package applies to title, tax, fraud and every known problem. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title "evidenced by" the Company share register (DD-012); Seller expressly says Buyer has not done its own verification | Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extracts, PPSR search over shares, review of constitution and any shareholder agreement/options; completion deliverables (transfer, certificates, register update, PPSR releases); fundamental title warranty + indemnity | **Action item for Buyer.** A company-maintained register is not conclusive, and the Seller has pointedly disclaimed any Buyer verification. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | "Settled" under the general regime | Full tax warranties plus a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or 100%, SOL+6–12 months, no basket); IP warranties on ownership, chain of title (Ironquay), no infringement; tax/IP outside general cap and knowledge qualifier | **Reject.** Nothing has been "settled" — no tax or IP terms appear in the package, and the general regime is the wrong home for them. |

---

## Overall assessment

The package is not "fair and balanced". Read together, items 001–007 and 014 produce a warranty regime in which almost nothing is claimable (blanket disclosure + constructive knowledge + single low cap + short period + no fraud carve-out), while items 008–013 leave every known DD problem (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar — roughly AUD 4.1m of identified exposure plus a ~30% revenue contract) sitting with the Buyer post-Completion.

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Riverlark discharge and Bluefen consent as hard Completion conditions/deliverables (009, 008).
2. Category separation, fundamental/tax carve-outs and fraud carve-out (014, 004, 005, 016).
3. Disclosure and knowledge qualifiers (006, 007).
4. Specific indemnities and price mechanics for the known items (010, 011, 012, 013).
5. Cap/basket/time economics (001, 002, 003) — negotiate last, once the structural points are fixed.

**Immediate Buyer actions:** order ASIC/PPSR searches (015); request bring-down of the data room and DD-006 investigation status to today; request payroll-tax/super analysis on the bonuses; ask Seller to confirm in writing which clauses it says the Buyer has "cleared" and on what basis.
